title: ADAS Sensor Calibrations: Customer Acceptance of a Customer-Pay Calibration
content:
## Acceptance rule

A customer-pay ADAS Sensor Calibrations order rests on the customer's acceptance of the calibration quote, and the customer accepts it by paying the acceptance amount. An accepted customer-pay calibration completed in-house posts its calibration charge at the calibration quote the customer accepted. Whatever an accepted order still owes is paid on completion by one of the tier's accepted payment methods.

The amount a customer pays to accept a calibration is fixed only after the order carries the goodwill write-off owed against its alignment correction charge.

Stated the other way round: until the order carries the goodwill write-off owed against its alignment correction charge, the acceptance amount is not yet a fixed figure.

## Points of the rule

| Question | Answer from the rule |
|---|---|
| What does a customer-pay order's agreement rest on? | The customer's acceptance of the calibration quote. |
| How does the customer accept? | By paying the acceptance amount. |
| At what figure is the calibration charge posted when the accepted calibration is completed in-house? | At the calibration quote the customer accepted. |
| What happens to whatever the accepted order still owes? | It is paid on completion by one of the tier's accepted payment methods. |

## The customer's acceptance payment: `pay_calibration_acceptance_f9e8bcf7`

**Capability.** With `pay_calibration_acceptance_f9e8bcf7` the customer accepts the sensor calibration on their own customer-pay calibration order by paying the acceptance amount. One call books a single customer payment, dated today, on the calibration order named, for the amount given and by the method given. What is owed on the order falls by exactly that amount, the payment appears in the order's calibration money history as a customer payment, and it stands as the customer's acceptance of the calibration.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks `pay_calibration_acceptance_f9e8bcf7` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `adas_order_id` | Reference number of the customer's calibration order, as read to the customer by the desk from the calibration order lookup | Id |
| `amount_usd` | The acceptance amount in US dollars | A positive amount with 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent; charged and stored exactly as given |
| `payment_method` | How the customer pays | One of: `card` — the customer pays with a debit or credit card, including over the phone; `cash` — the customer hands over cash at the center; `check` — the customer pays with a personal check at the center; `remittance` — only for an insurer glass program paying under its own remittance, never for a customer paying for themselves |

**Return.** A successful call returns a receipt carrying the payment's reference number, which the customer can quote afterwards:
- `status` — the text "accepted" when the payment was booked;
- `adas_entry_id` — reference number of the payment;
- `adas_order_id` — the calibration order accepted;
- `payer_kind` — always "customer";
- `payment_method` — the method used;
- `amount_usd` — the amount paid, USD, 2 decimal places;
- `entry_date` — the business date of the payment, YYYY-MM-DD.
